chunks: (Moses continued): "Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers before you."
ai.seo_question: Who is the Lord of the fathers in the Quran?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse highlights the continuity of divine monotheism (Tawhid) as Moses (AS) confronts Pharaoh, asserting that the God of the present is the same Lord of the patriarchs. Shia scholarship often views this as a foundational proof for the unbroken chain of prophetic guidance, linking the current revelation directly to the primordial covenant with the forefathers.
